name: Cholon
summary: The Chinese district of Saigon. Larry remembers off-duty visits to the French swimming pool there — the setting of the pool photographs VN-0004 and VN-0005, where he swam with Ron Tototz and a friend whose name he can no longer recall.
researchNotes: The 'French swimming pool' most plausibly refers to the Cercle Sportif–style colonial pool facilities that survived into the American period; period Saigon guides and veteran accounts of Cholon recreation spots could identify the specific pool and corroborate the English FIRST AID signage visible in VN-0004/VN-0005. 2026-08-23 (giscus-stories-c18118999): Larry places the swimming pool "near Binh Choi, which is south of the airport near Cholon" — a locating detail for the pool of VN-0004/VN-0005 that no previous account gave. "Binh Choi" is phonetic and not yet matched to a period place name; south of Tân Sơn Nhứt toward Chợ Lớn is the area implied. 2026-09-05: an unplaced fragment — 'I met some Thai soldiers that were different personalities. This may have been by the pool in Cholon' (data/recollections/giscus-vn-0041-c18308745.json). His son records that this was a separate story told while looking at a mountain photograph, not a caption for it; kept here because the pool is the only place he attaches to it. Thai military personnel in South Vietnam in 1964–65 were few (an air contingent from September 1964), which makes the encounter datable in principle. Also on 2026-09-05 he placed VN-0076, a street corner with bilingual Chinese–Vietnamese shop signs, at the Continental in Saigon; the signage reads more like this district. His placement stands on the photograph; the signage is noted there.
